name: freshwater_discus
story: Discus tank (6 adult discus plus corydoras and planted corners) in the living room of a flat in Bologna, November. 120 L, cheap 100 W heater, no chiller (enableCool left true by mistake, harmless). Central heating runs 6-8 and 17-23 only, so nights are cold, and a cold snap hits in week 2. Weekly 25% water changes with tap water that is colder than the tank. Cheap heater later develops a stuck internal thermostat, a loose probe connector coincides with it, a power cut, an ich treatment at 30 C, a welded relay, ADC drift, a child pulling out a probe, and finally a dead heater.

events.note: Owner airs the room at night, window left open
Weekly 25% change, tap water roughly tempered by hand
Powerhead/pump switch-on EMI glitch on one probe
Owner in a hurry, uses cold winter tap water, 12 K colder than tank
Probe lifted out during glass cleaning and forgotten on the rim
Cold snap, family away for a long weekend, heating off
Neighbour does the weekly change, uses cold tap
Neighbourhood blackout at night in a cold room, tank cools
Weekly change
Owner raises setpoint to 30 C for an ich treatment
Cheap heater's internal bimetal thermostat sticks closed, invisible while the controller cuts power
Loose probe connector after tank wiring is touched; one probe open, sensor fault, fail-safe, stuck heater is now unregulated
Owner notices the alarm and reseats the connector
Heater replaced by a new unit
Probe 1 slowly drifts warm from moisture ingress in the cable joint
Probe 0 frozen reading
Probe 0 recovers by itself
Ich treatment finished, back to normal setpoint
Owner lengthens photoperiod for plants
Heater relay contacts weld after many switchings, controller cannot cut heater
Relay board replaced
Probe 1 replaced, drift removed
3.3V rail sags (failing USB supply), all probes read cooler together
Power supply swapped
Family lunch, room heated and crowded
Heater element burns out
New heater installed
Child pulls a probe out of the water and leaves it hanging
Probe cable pinched under the lid
Lid adjusted, cable freed
Controller reset by an accidental plug bump

expect: Controller alone cannot break discus at 29 C: normal heat cycling with hysteresis 0.5; no chiller so enableCool true is harmless but any overtemp cannot be fixed actively.

FALSE ALARMS: hardcoded overtemp>27.5 and undertemp<22.5 are marine thresholds; discus sit at 28.5-30.5 C, so overtemp alarm should fire permanently from t=0 and during the ich treatment (30 C). This is a threshold-config issue to flag, not a real fault; the alarm becomes useless noise and masks real overheating.

Cold snap (h240-312, room about 12 C) plus cold water changes: 100 W heater is marginal (UA 5 W/K at 17 K delta); expect temp sag below 28 and possibly stress, heater duty near 100 percent, actuator stall alarm risk; blackout at h300 can drop tank towards 25-26 C and must recover without overshoot.

h400-430: stuck heater thermostat is harmless until sensor fault at h410; in fail-safe the heater is powered and only its stuck internal thermostat (never opens) regulates, so temp climbs above 31-32 C; the firmware must flag probe fault promptly; this is the real danger window. Welded heat relay at h520 similar: temp should rise to the heater internal set point about 32 C, welded relay alarm expected.

Probe faults (open, short, stuck, drift, out-of-water, EMI spike) must give sensorFault and fail-safe, short spikes should be filtered; out-of-water probes read room temp, must be detected as discordant; adc_gain 0.97 common-mode shift of about 0.9 C must be caught by ADC reference check or at least not drive overheating; heater dead at h600 must trigger heater stall alarm and undertemp drift.
